$comment: Sprint 52 / FU-license-audit-tool (Sprint 30) — curated allowlist for
third-party NuGet package licenses. Maps SPDX-style ids to whether the
license is permissive enough for v2's posture per audit-checklist-2026 SEC-DEP-3.
Conservative posture: anything not on this list is flagged. The allowlist is
deliberately narrow to force an explicit operator decision on edge cases
rather than silently admitting unknown licenses.
How to add a license: append below, AND add a one-sentence rationale in the
'rationale' map. Bump the version. Commit message MUST link the PR / issue
where the legal review happened. Per-package overrides (when nuspec metadata
is missing or wrong) live in the 'package_license_overrides' map below; each
override carries a rationale string referencing the upstream LICENSE source.
Out-of-allowlist examples (intentionally not allowed): GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0,
AGPL-3.0, LGPL-2.1, LGPL-3.0, MPL-1.1, MPL-2.0 (case-by-case), CC-BY-NC-*,
any 'commercial' / 'proprietary' / 'unknown' designation.
Sprint 57 update: triaged the 9 candidate findings from Sprint 52's first
audit. Added PostgreSQL to allowed (BSD-style, MIT-compatible); added per-
package overrides for FuncyDown (MIT), HdrHistogram (BSD-2-Clause),
FSharp.UMX (MIT), OneOf (MIT), xunit.abstractions (Apache-2.0). NBomber
6.1.0 is a P0 finding — the package's bundled LICENSE is the NBomber
Commercial Subscription Agreement, NOT MIT (csproj comment was wrong).
Documented under SEC-DEP-3 in audit-checklist-2026.md; see also
license-allowlist-rationale.md for full triage notes.

alias_normalisations.$comment: Map free-form license-strings observed in NuGet metadata onto canonical SPDX ids.

$comment: Map of (package-id-lowercase) -> { license: SPDX-id, rationale: string }
for packages whose .nuspec metadata is missing, wrong, or maps via a
licenseUrl shape the run-license-audit.ps1 url-pattern table doesn't
currently recognise. Each entry MUST cite the upstream LICENSE file as
evidence so the audit-trail survives package version bumps.
Note: this map is consumed by run-license-audit.ps1 only AFTER the
nuspec resolution loop. If a package version's nuspec already resolves
cleanly to a SPDX id on the allowlist, the override is ignored. Override
kicks in for status='url-only' / 'no-license-metadata' / 'no-nuspec'.
If the run-license-audit.ps1 script is later extended to consult this
map, it will read it via the JSON shape below. Until that wiring lands,
the report's triage section references this allowlist as the authority
and operators eyeball-check each finding against the override entry.

fsharp.umx.rationale: fsprojects standard MIT license. nuspec has neither <license> nor <licenseUrl>; license confirmed from https://github.com/fsprojects/FSharp.UMX repo licence display (LICENSE file in master).

funcydown.rationale: G DATA Software CyberDefense AG MIT license. nuspec has licenseUrl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GDATASoftwareAG/FuncyDown/master/LICENSE; LICENSE file opens 'MIT License Copyright (c) 2019 G DATA Software'.

hdrhistogram.rationale: Dual-licensed: primary release is CC0 / public domain; author Lee Campbell additionally provides BSD-2-Clause for those who prefer it. nuspec has licenseUrl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HdrHistogram/HdrHistogram.NET/master/LICENSE.txt. Pinning to BSD-2-Clause so we have a SPDX-mappable allowlisted entry.

oneof.rationale: Harry McIntyre MIT license. nuspec has licenseUrl https://github.com/mcintyre321/OneOf/blob/master/licence.md (note: 'licence' British spelling); file content is the MIT License with 'Copyright (c) 2016 Harry McIntyre'.

xunit.abstractions.rationale: Matches xunit.core posture: Apache-2.0 majority + MIT for imported dotnet/core-setup chunks. nuspec has licenseUrl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xunit/xunit/master/license.txt; the existing url-pattern table in run-license-audit.ps1 misses this because the pattern is *github.com/xunit/*LICENSE (case-sensitive 'LICENSE' suffix) but the URL ends in 'license.txt' (lowercase).

nbomber.rationale: P0 FINDING — NBomber 6.1.0's bundled LICENSE file is the 'NBOMBER LICENSE AGREEMENT Version 2.0' (commercial subscription terms; 'limited, non-exclusive, non-sublicensable, non-transferable, revocable' license tied to a paid Activation Key). The csproj comment in tests/NickERP.Perf.Tests/NickERP.Perf.Tests.csproj that calls it 'MIT-licensed' was incorrect. NBomber.Contracts is Apache-2.0 (separate package) but the runtime engine NBomber requires a paid commercial subscription. NOT added to overrides — must be resolved by either purchasing a subscription or replacing with a permissive-licensed alternative (e.g. dotnet-bombardier, k6 via HTTP runner, or a hand-rolled NBomber.Contracts-only harness). See SEC-DEP-3 in audit-checklist-2026.md for the resolution decision.

nbomber.contracts.rationale: nbomber.contracts (Apache-2.0) is a separate package from nbomber (commercial). The contracts library is OK to use under Apache-2.0 terms; only the nbomber runtime triggers the proprietary subscription requirement.

rationale.MIT: Permissive; commercial-use OK; no copyleft; default for .NET ecosystem.
rationale.Apache-2.0: Permissive; explicit patent grant; commercial-use OK; widely used by Microsoft / Google libraries.
rationale.BSD-3-Clause: Permissive; commercial-use OK; common for academic-origin libraries.
rationale.BSD-2-Clause: Permissive; commercial-use OK; minimal restrictions vs BSD-3.
rationale.ISC: Permissive; equivalent to BSD-2/MIT in effect.
rationale.MS-PL: Microsoft Public License; permissive for commercial use; used by some legacy MS NuGets.
rationale.MS-EULA: Microsoft .NET Library license terms; covers framework / first-party Microsoft NuGets like System.* and Microsoft.* packages.
rationale.PostgreSQL: PostgreSQL License (BSD-style, MIT-compatible per the PostgreSQL Global Development Group's official wording: 'similar to the BSD or MIT licenses'); covers Npgsql + Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL, the canonical .NET driver for our Postgres backend.
